assessment.nobel_worthiness: Nitrogenase is the central enzyme of biological nitrogen fixation, and its structure and mechanism are a physical-chemical problem of the first rank: electron delivery, ATP-gated conformational coupling, and substrate reduction at an unprecedented metal cluster (FeMo-cofactor with its interstitial carbide). The structural work made the mechanism visible, which is the kind of mechanism-first biochemistry I weight most.
assessment.attribution: Rees led the crystallographic structure and cofactor analysis, Einsle's atomic-resolution structure established the central light atom, and Seefeldt (with Dean) defined the kinetic and mechanistic framework. Dean, Ribbe and others are also credible; with a three-laureate limit the allocation between structural and biochemical contributions is unresolved.
assessment.maturity: Structures spanning decades are independently confirmed by several groups, and the cofactor composition is settled; the catalytic cycle and the nature of the substrate-binding state are still being refined, so the story is mature but not closed.
uncertainties: Which intermediate states of the catalytic cycle are firmly established is still debated.
Credit between early structural pioneers (not all credited here) and later cofactor work, and between structure and biochemistry, is contested.
I am relying on my own recollection of the literature and have not verified details independently.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Serial femtosecond crystallography at X-ray free-electron lasers turned diffraction-before-destruction into a practical method, giving room-temperature structures of microcrystals and time-resolved views of reactions in proteins. It makes dynamic chemical processes visible in three dimensions, a methodological advance with clear mechanistic payoff.
assessment.attribution: Hajdu originated the diffraction-before-destruction concept, Chapman led the first demonstrations and methods development, and Schlichting contributed key time-resolved and instrument work. Fromme's role in membrane protein crystallography and Spence and Neutze, not credited here, complicate a three-person configuration.
assessment.maturity: The method is well reproduced at several facilities, though the strongest scientific returns, such as general time-resolved enzymology, are still accumulating. Timing is reasonable but perhaps slightly early.
uncertainties: Whether the prize would be for the method or for particular biological discoveries made with it.
Crowded priority claims around the originating concept and the first experiments.
Radiation-damage and time-resolution artifacts need careful consideration in individual studies.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Proton-coupled electron transfer is a unifying physical principle in respiratory enzymes, photosynthesis and molecular electrocatalysis. A formal theory plus well-defined model systems turned concerted proton-electron movement into a predictive concept in chemistry and biology.
assessment.attribution: Hammes-Schiffer provided the theoretical framework, Mayer the thermochemical and bond-strength picture of concerted transfer, and Meyer early inorganic PCET studies. Nocera is also a strong claimant, particularly for artificial photosynthesis, so the three-person boundary is genuinely uncertain.
assessment.maturity: The concept is broadly confirmed across systems, but it is partly a line of work rather than a single attributable discovery, and I should weigh that carefully.
uncertainties: Whether the committee would see this as one discovery or a collection of related advances.
Allocation of credit between theory and experiment and between Meyer, Mayer and Nocera.
My own research proximity requires care in avoiding overweighting.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Multidimensional solution NMR methods, including heteronuclear experiments, isotope labeling strategies and relaxation-based approaches, allow structure and dynamics of large biomolecules to be studied in solution. The impact on structural biology and on understanding conformational exchange is very large and lasting.
assessment.attribution: Bax, Kay and Clore are repeatedly decisive: Bax for triple-resonance and residual dipolar coupling methods, Kay for TROSY-based and relaxation dispersion approaches on large systems, and Clore for structure determination and sparsely populated states. Wagner and Palmer have comparable claims, and NMR was recognized earlier (Ernst 1991, Wüthrich 2002), which raises a question of whether this is a new prize.
assessment.maturity: Methods are very widely used and long confirmed, so maturity is high. The risk is overlap with the earlier NMR prizes rather than prematurity.
uncertainties: Whether the committee views this as sufficiently distinct from earlier recognized NMR work.
Distribution of credit among several leading groups.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Native mass spectrometry preserves non-covalent assemblies in the gas phase, giving stoichiometry, topology and ligand binding of intact protein complexes, including membrane proteins and their lipid interactions. It complements structural methods and supports mechanistic understanding.
assessment.attribution: Robinson pioneered large-complex and membrane protein work, Heck developed high-resolution and high-mass applications, and Chait contributed early methods and protein complex analysis. Loo and Gross have credible claims, and the 2002 mass spectrometry prize addressed ionization methods.
assessment.maturity: Established and reproducible, with growing adoption; the conceptual step beyond earlier ionization prizes may be viewed as an application rather than a new discovery.
uncertainties: Whether the committee considers this a sufficiently distinct advance from electrospray ionization.
Question of fidelity of gas-phase structures to solution states.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Energy landscape theory reframed protein folding as a funneled physical process, explaining how proteins escape Levinthal's paradox, while experimental mapping of transition states connected theory to kinetics. It is a physical-mechanism achievement with deep conceptual influence.
assessment.attribution: Wolynes and Onuchic, with Bryngelson, developed the funnel and landscape framework; Fersht provided experimental kinetic and mutational methods. Dill's contribution on hydrophobic collapse and Bryngelson's early role are not fully accommodated by a three-person limit.
assessment.maturity: The concept is widely accepted, but it is more a general theoretical framework than a single testable discovery, and its predictive reach for design is partly eclipsed by recent prizes in structure prediction.
uncertainties: Whether the framework is a single attributable discovery.
Relation to the 2024 recognition of protein design and structure prediction.
Credit allocation between theory and experiment.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Quantitative study of electron tunneling through proteins explained how redox enzymes, including respiratory ones, move electrons over long distances, with distance and driving-force dependences tested in engineered metalloprotein systems. It sits close to the physical basis of biological energy conversion.
assessment.attribution: Gray and Winkler's work is tightly linked, with Marcus theory and the earlier recognition of Marcus (1992) and Taube providing the background. Credit may need to include others working on tunneling pathways (e.g., Beratan, Onuchic), who are not in the supplied names.
assessment.maturity: Mature and widely confirmed, though the main results are decades old, which makes recognition more of a retrospective than a timely one.
uncertainties: Relation to the earlier Marcus prize and possibility of being viewed as an elaboration.
Absent credited names for the theoretical pathway models.
My own field proximity requires caution.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Liquid-liquid phase separation as an organizing principle of intracellular compartments has changed how cell biology and biophysical chemistry think about membraneless organelles. It brings physical chemistry to the cell.
assessment.attribution: Hyman and Brangwynne gave the founding demonstration with P granules, and Rosen's multivalent-system work offered a quantitative physical basis. Pappu and Mittag contributed on sequence determinants, so a three-person boundary leaves out important contributors.
assessment.maturity: Influence is large, but the functional significance in vivo and the criteria for what counts as phase separation are still contested, so maturity is less secure.
uncertainties: Ongoing debate on the physiological relevance and the rigor of in-cell evidence.
Whether it is a chemistry or a physiology and cell biology achievement.
Credit boundaries among several leaders.
